newsitem.title: JAPAN: U.S. Treasuries little changed, undertone easier.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasuries little changed, undertone easier.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries stood ittle changed by Tokyo midday on Tuesday, with the market undertone slightly easier after overnight losses, traders said.

Trading was quiet ahead of the first leg of a two-day Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting starting Tuesday and the National Association of Purchasing Management (NAPM) data due for release at 1400 GMT, they said.

"The market is unwilling to take fresh position before NAPM and jobs data (on Thursday)," a senior Japanese bank trader said. "But it seems the market is more comfortable about creating short positions, given this mood."
The 6-5/8 percent 30-year bond stood at 97-29/32, yielding 6.79 percent, compared with 97-30/32 in New York.
Strong housing sales and an improved Chicago purchasing managers' survey pushed down prices in New York on Monday.
"Although, people are not expecting the Fed to tighten credit at the FOMC meetings, a wait-and-see mood spread (in Asia)," a Japanese brokerage manager said.
"The market is expected to react gently to the results of NAPM data. But even if the market tests prices downwards, I don't expect them to fall steeply and continuously," the manager said.
U.S. economists in a Reuters survey conducted last Friday expected a reading of 56.4 for June compared to 57.1 in May.
A reading above 50.0 indicates an expanding manufacturing economy, according to NAPM.
The T-bond futures market inched up in thin trade, but the market lacked direction throughout the morning.
The September T-bond futures contract rose 2/32 to 111-4/32 by midday from the previous close. It was moving in a range of 111-2/32 to 111-7/32.
